questions.corrige_markdown: **First aid** is the **immediate (emergency) help or care given to a victim of an accident or sudden illness before a doctor or professional medical help arrives**, in order to **save life, prevent the condition from getting worse and promote recovery**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain the first aid to be administered to a victim bitten by a snake on the limb. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Keep the victim calm and still** (reassure him or her) and **lay the victim down**, because movement and fear speed up the spread of the venom.
2. **Keep the bitten limb still**, and remove rings, watches and tight clothing near the bite before swelling begins.
3. **Apply a firm (not too tight) bandage or tie a tourniquet (a band) 5 to 10 cm above the bite**, loosening it every 15 to 20 minutes, to **slow the flow of venom** to the heart.
4. **Wash the wound gently with clean water and soap** and cover it with a clean dressing; **do not cut, suck or apply herbs** to the wound.
5. **Take the victim quickly to a hospital** for **anti-venom (antiserum) injection**; if possible note the type of snake.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Describe the life cycle of the malaria parasite (plasmodium). *(8 marks)*

(ii) How can the spread of malaria be prevented? *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Life cycle of Plasmodium** (in two hosts: the female *Anopheles* mosquito (vector) and man):

1. An **infected female Anopheles mosquito bites a person** and injects **saliva containing sporozoites** into the blood.
2. The sporozoites **travel in the blood to the liver**, enter the **liver cells**, and **multiply by asexual reproduction** into many **merozoites**. The liver cells burst.
3. The merozoites **enter the red blood cells**, feed on haemoglobin and **multiply** again, forming more merozoites; the red blood cells **burst** and release merozoites together with **toxins**, which cause the **fever and shivering** (every 48 to 72 hours); the merozoites invade new red blood cells.
4. Some merozoites develop into **male and female gametocytes**, which remain in the blood.
5. When a **female Anopheles mosquito bites** an infected person, it **sucks up the gametocytes with the blood**.
6. In the **stomach of the mosquito**, the gametocytes **develop into gametes, which fuse (fertilisation)** to form a **zygote**, which develops into an **oocyst** on the stomach wall.
7. The oocyst **divides** to produce many **sporozoites**, which **burst out and move to the salivary glands** of the mosquito.
8. The mosquito is now infective and **injects sporozoites into the next person it bites**, and the cycle starts again.

(ii) **Prevention of the spread of malaria**:
1. **Destroy the mosquito**: **drain stagnant water and fill ditches**, clear bushes, **cover water containers** and clean the surroundings to **remove breeding places**.
2. **Spray insecticides** on walls and in rooms and **pour oil or larvicides on stagnant water** to kill larvae and pupae; **introduce larvae-eating fish** (biological control).
3. **Use mosquito nets (insecticide-treated nets)**, put **screens (wire gauze) on windows and doors**, and use repellents and mosquito coils.
4. **Wear long-sleeved clothes in the evening** and avoid being outside at dusk and at night when mosquitoes bite.
5. **Treat patients promptly** with **antimalarial drugs** (for example artemisinin-based drugs) to **destroy the parasite in the blood** and reduce the source of infection; take **prophylactic drugs** (for example in pregnancy or when visiting an endemic area).
6. **Health education** of the population about the above measures.
